context.text: This is the Class II U.S. Senate seat held by Jack Reed, who first took office in 1997. Reed defeated Connor Burbridge and Luis Daniel Muñoz in the September 9, 2026 Democratic primary, 76.8%-13.5%-9.7%. Raymond McKay ran unopposed for the Republican nomination after Allen Waters withdrew. Michael Bahry is running as an independent; a fourth candidate, Jon Lindley (independent), withdrew or was disqualified before the general election.

summary.text: Jack Reed is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to a sixth full term in the U.S. Senate. He previously served in the Rhode Island State Senate (1985-1991) and the U.S. House (1991-1997), and is the ranking member of the Senate Armed Services Committee.

background.text: Born in Providence, Rhode Island, in 1949. Earned a bachelor's degree from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point (1971), a Master of Public Policy from Harvard's Kennedy School (1973), and a J.D. from Harvard Law School (1982).
Served in the U.S. Army from 1967 to 1979, and later worked as a professor and lawyer.
Served in the Rhode Island State Senate from 1985 to 1991, then in the U.S. House of Representatives for Rhode Island's 2nd District from 1991 to 1997.

record.text: For the 2025-2026 Congress, serves as Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, Ranking Member of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government, and a member of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs and the Select Committee on Intelligence.
Chaired the Senate Armed Services Committee and the Appropriations Subcommittee on the Legislative Branch during the 2023-2024 Congress.

candidates.name: Raymond McKay

summary.text: Raymond McKay is the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate. He is a retired U.S. Army veteran and former City of Warwick telecommunications manager who also ran for this seat's Republican nomination in 2024.

background.text: Born in Providence, Rhode Island, on October 11, 1960; graduated from Hope High School.

Served in the U.S. Army from 1981 to 1992, working on electronic maintenance for the Pershing missile system in West Germany and later as a programmer at Fort Gordon; discharged at the rank of Sergeant.
Worked for 26 years as the network and telecommunications manager for the City of Warwick.
Served as president of the Rhode Island Republican Assembly for 10 years and has worked as a campaign manager on Rhode Island political campaigns.

priorities.text: Curbing federal government spending, which he says drives inflation and economic pressure on Rhode Islanders.
Securing the border and enforcing immigration law.
Strengthening Social Security and Medicare, and supporting veterans and the military.

positions.summary: Says the country must secure its borders and enforce its laws.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities are drawn from McKay's 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (for a prior run for this same seat); he has not completed a 2026 survey and no updated policy page was found on his 2026 campaign site.

summary.text: Michael Bahry is an independent candidate for U.S. Senate, a Providence-based former construction executive and current theology instructor who is campaigning primarily on ending U.S. involvement in foreign wars and congressional term limits.

background.text: Native Rhode Islander; career included work as a laborer, carpenter, construction executive and business owner.
Founded the nonprofit Fifty-Three: Five in 2014, which provides food and support to families and the homeless in Providence.
Earned two graduate degrees from Providence College: a Master of Theological Studies (2017) and a Master of Arts in Biblical Studies (2022).
Works as a theology instructor at Salve Regina University.

priorities.text: Ending U.S. participation in what he calls "endless wars," saying it makes the world less safe rather than more.
Running as an independent so he can vote issue-by-issue without party loyalty.
Addressing the national debt, which he says has been driven up by career politicians.

positions.summary: Calls the war in Gaza a tragedy and campaigns for peace rather than continued military involvement in the conflict.
